<a id="src-engine-combat-coverage-test-ts"></a>

### src/engine/combat/coverage.test.ts

Everything in combat, once each: every skill, boss move, assist, status, item, gear piece, sheet of music, enemy and boss. The mechanics tests (combat.test.ts) check *what* each rule does; this file checks that *nothing* in the tables breaks: no throw, no NaN, no runaway fight, no "undefined" in the battle log. It reads every id list, so new content is covered the moment it's added.

- Source: [src/engine/combat/coverage.test.ts](../../../src/engine/combat/coverage.test.ts)
- Imports: core: [helpers](core.md#src-core-helpers-ts), [ids/band](core.md#src-core-ids-band-ts), [ids/characters](core.md#src-core-ids-characters-ts), [ids/combat](core.md#src-core-ids-combat-ts), [ids/enemies](core.md#src-core-ids-enemies-ts), [ids/items](core.md#src-core-ids-items-ts), [rng](core.md#src-core-rng-ts), [types/index](core.md#src-core-types-index-ts) · content: [data](content.md#src-content-data-ts) · engine: [combat/statuses](engine.md#src-engine-combat-statuses-ts), [combat/turns](engine.md#src-engine-combat-turns-ts), [index](engine.md#src-engine-index-ts)

<a id="tools-parity-content-test-ts"></a>

### tools/parity/content.test.ts

Content oracle: every typed table, mapped back through the documented renames, deep-equals the legacy table it came from. Function-valued fields are compared by position only (both sides become "&lt;fn>"); their behavior is covered by the engine oracle. Data that moved (bounty gold, journal text, hint places, note pitches, passives) is checked against its legacy source.

- Source: [tools/parity/content.test.ts](../../../tools/parity/content.test.ts)
- Imports: core: [ids/combat](core.md#src-core-ids-combat-ts), [ids/enemies](core.md#src-core-ids-enemies-ts), [ids/story](core.md#src-core-ids-story-ts), [ids/world](core.md#src-core-ids-world-ts) · content: [data](content.md#src-content-data-ts) · tools: [parity/driver](tools.md#tools-parity-driver-ts), [parity/legacy](tools.md#tools-parity-legacy-ts)
- Packages: `vitest`
- Suites: “content parity with legacy v1 tables”

<a id="tools-parity-engine-test-ts"></a>

### tools/parity/engine.test.ts

Engine parity: the TypeScript engine must replay the whole corpus draw-for-draw like legacy v1. On failure, the message names the fight, the first differing path, and the events around it. See docs/adr/0003-determinism-and-parity.md.

- Source: [tools/parity/engine.test.ts](../../../tools/parity/engine.test.ts)
- Imports: tools: [parity/corpus](tools.md#tools-parity-corpus-ts), [parity/driver](tools.md#tools-parity-driver-ts), [parity/legacyAdapter](tools.md#tools-parity-legacyadapter-ts), [parity/micro](tools.md#tools-parity-micro-ts), [parity/tsAdapter](tools.md#tools-parity-tsadapter-ts)
- Packages: `vitest`
- Suites: “engine parity with legacy v1”

<a id="tools-parity-properties-test-ts"></a>

### tools/parity/properties.test.ts

Properties of the TypeScript engine that the parity oracle doesn't cover: - determinism: the same seed replays the same fight, with no hidden global state; - presentation: folding Heart events (hpAfter) always reproduces every actor's real Heart, so the UI can animate events without ever reading the battle's final state.

- Source: [tools/parity/properties.test.ts](../../../tools/parity/properties.test.ts)
- Imports: core: [rng](core.md#src-core-rng-ts), [types/index](core.md#src-core-types-index-ts) · tools: [parity/corpus](tools.md#tools-parity-corpus-ts), [parity/driver](tools.md#tools-parity-driver-ts), [parity/legacyAdapter](tools.md#tools-parity-legacyadapter-ts), [parity/tsAdapter](tools.md#tools-parity-tsadapter-ts)
- Packages: `vitest`
- Suites: “engine properties”

<a id="tools-parity-transcripts-test-ts"></a>

### tools/parity/transcripts.test.ts

Transcript oracle: ported scenes show the player exactly what v1 showed and leave the save in the same state. v1 runs in jsdom with its UI functions replaced by recorders; both sides use a constant random value (so every pick/chance lands the same way) and fights stubbed as wins.
